articles.title: Apple hit with $5.7 billion verdict over Taptic Engine patent infringement
articles.summary: Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions. Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents. more…

articles.title: I turned my Android phone’s annoying AI button into its most powerful shortcut key
articles.summary: Nowadays, you can’t avoid phones that boast AI features . Smartphone launches are becoming more AI-centric; hardware frequently takes a back seat, and each brand has its own flavor of AI assistant. Nowhere is this more apparent than when phones come with dedicated AI buttons. My phone’s AI button was its least attractive feature. However, when I realized I could program it to perform a range of non-AI tasks, it became the button I use most on my device.

articles.title: 5 of my favorite Android features you won’t find on Samsung or Pixel phones
articles.summary: It’s no secret that the Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel brands get a lot of attention from the media and Android fans alike. There are several reasons for this, including better software update support than the competition and a large selection of exclusive hardware and software features. For those in North America, it’s also because these are the two largest Android brands left. While it’s true that Samsung and Google have many exclusive features, they aren’t the only ones. Below are a few features that both brands either miss entirely or don’t do as well, all of which I would personally love to see come to more devices.
articles.title_zh: 5 of my favorite Android features you won’t find on Samsung or Pixel phones
articles.summary_zh: It’s no secret that the Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel brands get a lot of attention from the media and Android fans alike. There are several reasons for this, including better software update support than the competition and a large selection of exclusive hardware and software features. For those in North America, it’s also because these are the two largest Android brands left. While it’s true that Samsung and Google have many exclusive features, they aren’t the only ones. Below are a few features that both brands either miss entirely or don’t do as well, all of which I would personally love to see come to more devices.

articles.title: I tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL against the Pixel 8 Pro. Here’s why it’s time to finally upgrade
articles.summary: I’ve defended Pixels for a few years now. Not because I’m beholden to any manufacturer, but because I genuinely appreciate the effort Google’s made to improve its phones. At one point, I was kicked off Team Pixel because I didn’t appreciate the early Tensor performance and thought the company was headed in the wrong direction. The Pixel 8 Pro changed that perception for me, and it was the first time I felt Google could actually deliver on its vision for Pixel. I’ve been a fan of the phone ever since, and I’ve told people to resist the temptation to upgrade.

articles.title: I used to love foldable phones. Now, I can’t stand them
articles.summary: Just as they have with their inner screens, foldables have divided the user base into two camps — either you find regular phones too simplistic to go back to, or you just don’t want to see your phone fold in half anymore. There is no other realization you have after living with a foldable. And the title must’ve given away that I fall under the second category. I used to be a book-style foldable die-hard, but as the novelty wore off, its flaws became glaring by the day. And no, I’m not concerned by foldables coming with one less rear camera or a more fragile exterior. My problem is more fundamental. I just can’t fathom the very idea of a device deploying complicated and delicate (not to mention expensive) mechanics to do two things at once when I’m not convinced it excels at either.

articles.title: 7 surprisingly useful ways to use Google Lens beyond basic search
articles.summary: Google Lens is a powerful tool that makes it incredibly easy to understand the world around you. Just point your phone’s camera at a subject, and it gives you the relevant information. And because Google Lens is deeply integrated with Gemini, you can follow up with any doubts or questions to get answers. You may already know about Google Lens or use it on your phone to identify plants and animals, translate text, solve Math problems, or even find what’s on your screen. But its usefulness doesn’t end there. Google Lens has plenty of other use cases that you should know about.

articles.title: AI Safety Concerns Put Congress on the Spot
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Don Beyer of Virginia tells Bloomberg This Weekend that recent AI incidents have increased the urgency for federal safeguards, including safety testing and mandatory reporting of serious problems involving advanced models. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Beyer, co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus, says Congress should create a regulatory structure that combines federal oversight with technical expertise from AI companies. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: Why Humanoid Robots Might Be the Future of Elder Care
articles.summary: The US spends roughly $400 billion a year on long-term care, and for every 100 people over 65, only four formal caregivers exist. Humanoid robots like Abi, built by Andromeda to provide emotional companionship for dementia patients, are an early attempt to ease that pressure. Andromeda COO Jennifer Haroon, Brookings researcher Gopi Goda, 1X Chief Designer Dar Sleeper, and Nvidia's Kimberly Powell discuss whether robots can truly help solve the elder care crisis, or whether the technology still has too far to go. (Source: Bloomberg)
